title: When two galaxies collide, their stars almost never hit each other

cover.alt: Computer simulation of two galaxies about to collide: a large fuzzy ball of stars with a smaller one below it on a dark grey background.
cover.credit: ESO/J. Barnes/Peirani et al. · CC BY 4.0

body: Matter in a galaxy is spread so thinly that when two galaxies run into each other, it isn’t a crash in the usual sense: the stars **almost never get close enough to collide**. Gravity still reshapes both galaxies, pulling out streams of stars and dragging them back together until they merge, which can take a billion years or more. What does collide is gas. Giant clouds run into each other, and the shocks set off bursts of new stars. Many astronomers think big mergers like this are the main way elliptical galaxies are made.

slides.alt: Computer simulation in grey: a small galaxy swings past a larger spiral, a long curved stream of stars is pulled out, and the small galaxy loops back and sinks into the larger one.
slides.caption: Computer simulation: two spiral galaxies swing past each other, fling out a stream of stars, then fall back together and merge. Made to explain a distant galaxy studied with Hubble and ESO’s VLT.
slides.credit: ESO/J. Barnes/Peirani et al. · CC BY 4.0 · excerpt

slides.heading: What a galaxy collision is like

left.label: Myth
left.text: Galaxies smash together like cars, and their stars crash into each other.

right.label: Fact
right.text: Stars almost never collide. Gas clouds do, and the shocks make new stars.

steps.label: Two galaxies pass close to each other
Gravity pulls out streams of stars and gas
Gas clouds collide and spark new stars
The pair settles into a single galaxy

slides.prompt: A galaxy merger takes far longer than a human lifetime. So how do astronomers study one?
slides.detail: They simulate colliding galaxies, as in the clip, and compare the results with real galaxies caught at different stages, including how their gas moves.

slides.question: What kind of galaxy do many astronomers think big mergers create?
slides.explanation: Many astronomers think major mergers are the main way elliptical galaxies are made; ellipticals are seen as the end products of big collisions.
